nodes.statement: Deutsch (2013, arXiv:1210.7439, Section 1.1 eqs. (1)-(2) pp. 2-4 and Section 1.2 p. 5) proposes to state physical laws as statements about which physical transformations (tasks) can be caused to happen and which cannot, in place of dynamical laws plus initial conditions, together with the composition principle (Section 1.2 p. 5), computation media (Section 2.6 eq. (9) pp. 13-14) and Einstein locality on composite substrates (Section 3.10 p. 33). This node records the proposal as published.

nodes.statement: Imported vocabulary, audited against Deutsch (2013, Section 1.1 eqs. (1)-(2) pp. 2-4) and Deutsch-Marletto (2015, Section 2 pp. 6-8): a task is a set of ordered input/output attribute pairs of a substrate; a constructor causes the transformation and retains its ability to do so again; a task is possible when the laws of nature impose no limit short of perfection on how accurately it can be performed and how well a constructor can retain its ability to perform it again, and not possible otherwise; Principle I (Section 2 p. 8) states that the state of a composite substrate S1 + S2 is the pair of states on S1 and S2 and a construction on S1 changes only the S1 state. The repository uses none of this vocabulary as a primitive.
nodes.bottleneck: Taking the possible and not-possible partition of tasks as primitive is a different foundational choice from the repository's admitted primitive PG-ROOT-DIFF-STRUCTURE and its replayed refusal predicates. No source derives either from the other.

nodes.statement: Formalized finite statement. For a finite set X and a report map q from X to R, two attributes A and B of X (nonemptiness is not needed) are separated by a deterministic task, meaning a function f from R to {0,1} with f(q(a))=0 on A and f(q(b))=1 on B, if and only if q(A) and q(B) are disjoint. Checked in Lean 4 over Finset for arbitrary types X and R with decidable equality on R: both directions and the biconditional; when q(A) and q(B) are disjoint the indicator of B on the union of A and B is constant on the fibers of q (HistoryReport.FiberConstant, the form PG-HISTORY-REPORT-CRITERION takes); and an exhaustive bitmask decision check over all (q, A, B) with nonempty attributes for 1<=|X|<=4 and 1<=|R|<=3. This matches the constructor-theoretic notion of distinguishable attributes only on its deterministic finite fragment: accuracy, repeatability and constructor existence are not modelled.
nodes.bottleneck: Checked in Lean 4 on Finset for all finite carriers and by the exhaustive check for |X|<=4, |R|<=3. Whether the finite condition deserves the name "distinguishable attributes" in the source's sense depends on the imported definition, which this repository does not adopt.

nodes.statement: Deutsch and Marletto (2015, arXiv:1405.5563) formulate a constructor theory of information by defining computation variables (Section 3 p. 9), clonable variables and information media (Section 4 eq. (3) p. 10) prior to distinguishability (Section 5 eq. (4) p. 11), avoiding the circularity of Section 1 eq. (1) p. 3. Section 7 (p. 20) and Section 8 (pp. 20-24) define superinformation media and derive non-distinguishability, no-cloning of non-orthogonal states, complementarity and unpredictability from Principles I-IX. This node records the paper as published.

nodes.statement: Imported principles, audited and corrected against Deutsch and Marletto (2015, arXiv:1405.5563, Sections 3-6 pp. 9-12): a computation variable is a set S of at least two possible attributes for which all permutation tasks are possible with side-effects (Section 3 p. 9); a variable S is clonable if the cloning task R_S(x0) = union_{x in S} {(x, x0) -> (x, x)} is possible with side-effects for some preparable blank attribute x0 (Section 4 eq. (3) p. 10); an information variable is a clonable computation variable, and an information medium is a substrate with at least one information variable (Section 4 p. 10). Distinguishability is defined afterward in Section 5 (eq. (4) p. 11) by mapping into an information variable, avoiding circularity, and every information variable is then shown to be distinguishable. Principle III (interoperability, Section 6 p. 12) states that the composite S1 + S2 of two substrates with information variables S1 and S2 is an information medium with information variable S1 x S2.
nodes.bottleneck: The interoperability principle (Principle III, Section 6 p. 12) constrains composite information variables to include S1 x S2 in the source's framework. It is not shown to select the Hilbert tensor product, local tomography or any positive cone, so it does not discharge FQ-GAP-TENSOR-UNIQUENESS.

nodes.statement: Imported definition, audited and corrected against Deutsch and Marletto (2015, arXiv:1405.5563, Section 6 pp. 14-18 and Section 7 p. 20): an information observable is an information variable X whose attributes satisfy double-complement closure x = u_x under distinguishability (Section 6, Principle VIII p. 16); a superinformation medium is an information medium with at least two information observables X and Y that contain only mutually disjoint attributes and whose union X union Y is not an information observable (Section 7 p. 20). Sections 8.1 and 8.3 (pp. 20-22) show under Principles III, IV, VI, VII, VIII and IX that X union Y is neither distinguishable nor clonable. The repository neither adopts this definition as a primitive nor claims that its finite carriers satisfy Principles I-IX.

nodes.statement: Finite statement over Q(i), checked in Lean 4 in the following narrowed form. Take the qubit with the six Pauli eigenstates as rays. (a) The explicit measure-and-prepare maps cloneZ, cloneX and cloneY (rho to the mixture of the two basis clones with weights Tr(P rho)) send each of |0>,|1>; |+>,|->; |+i>,|-i> to its own clone rho tensor rho; cloneZ is shown trace-preserving. (b) The exact relation |0><0|+|1><1| = |+><+|+|-><-| holds in Herm(2), and the difference of the two clone sums has entry -1/2 on |00><11| and |11><00|, so no additive map (hence no linear map) clones all four of |0>,|1>,|+>,|->. (c) The exact squared overlaps of the six states are 1 (equal), 0 (antipodal) or 1/2 (otherwise); for a rational x in [0,1], x <= x^2 forces x in {0,1}; and an exhaustive count over the 64 subsets of the six states shows that exactly 10 subsets are pairwise equal-or-orthogonal (the empty set, 6 singletons and 3 antipodal pairs) and that the maximal such subsets are the three antipodal pairs. In Lean "cloneable subset" in (c) is defined as pairwise equal-or-orthogonal.
nodes.bottleneck: Not proved in Lean: complete positivity of cloneZ, cloneX and cloneY, and trace preservation of cloneX and cloneY (only cloneZ is shown trace-preserving); that completely positive trace-preserving maps cannot decrease fidelity (x <= x^2 is a hypothesis of the arithmetic lemma, not derived); and the equivalence of the semantic notion "some CPTP map clones every state of the subset" with "pairwise equal or orthogonal" in either direction (the Lean classification takes the latter as the definition of cloneable). The link to the imported definition of a superinformation medium is a reading of definitions.

(8) p. 4) for two Stern-Gerlach interferometers interacting through Newtonian gravity phases delta phi_+- and delta phi_-+ (eqs. (2)-(4) p. 2). This node records both papers; no experiment is claimed to have been performed.

nodes.statement: Finite statement over Q(i), checked in Lean 4 for (a) to (c); (d) is not proved. For u in Q(i) (the Lean proofs of (a) and (b) do not use |u|=1), the two-qubit vector psi_u = (1,1,1,u)/2 has coefficient matrix M_u = [[1,1],[1,u]]/2 of determinant (u-1)/4. (a) psi_u is a product vector if and only if u=1. (b) The squared concurrence, defined as 4|det M|^2, equals |u-1|^2/4 for M_u; for u=(3+4i)/5, where |u|=1, it equals 1/5. (c) For all 2x2 matrices A and B over Q(i), det(A M B^T) = det(A) det(M) det(B), so det M = 0 implies det(A M B^T) = 0: local operations cannot raise a product vector to Schmidt rank 2; and diag(1,1,1,u) applied to the product vector (1,1,1,1)/2 gives psi_u. The physical inference from such entanglement to a non-classical mediator is imported, not part of this target.
nodes.bottleneck: Statement (d), an exact separating functional on the 4x4 density matrix relative to the product family in the form of DS-QM071, is not proved. The Lean module defines schmidtWitnessExpectation(M) = |det M|^2, a quadratic function of the amplitude matrix that vanishes on product vectors and is positive on psi_u for u != 1; that is a restatement of (a), not a linear functional on density matrices, and it is not shown to vanish on mixtures of product states or tied to DS-QM071. The rank inequality rank(A M B^T) <= rank(M) for general rank is stated only through the 2x2 determinant identity (preservation of det M = 0). No physical claim is attached.

nodes.statement: Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 for site-factorized operators. For a FiniteStrictPoset P on n points put one qubit (a single-site monoid M) at each point; an operator A : Fin n -> M is localized in a subset O of P when it is the identity outside O, so the Lean "algebra" of O is the set of elementary tensor operators localized in O, not the full matrix algebra on the qubits in O. (a) Isotony: O1 inside O2 and A localized in O1 imply A localized in O2. (b) Locality: if every point of O1 is spacelike to every point of O2, then O1 and O2 are disjoint and operators localized in O1 and in O2 commute under the sitewise product. (c) The spacelike relation of CausalOrder.lean is symmetric (spacelike_symm) and irreflexive (spacelike_irrefl) and not transitive: on the four-element N poset 0<2, 1<2, 1<3, points 1 and 0 are spacelike, 0 and 3 are spacelike, and 1<3 are related. records.summary: Deutsch and Marletto (2015, arXiv:1405.5563) formulate a constructor theory of information by defining computation variables (Section 3 p. 9), clonable variables and information media (Section 4 eq. (3) p. 10) prior to distinguishability (Section 5 eq. (4) p. 11), avoiding the circularity of Section 1 eq. (1) p. 3. Section 7 (p. 20) and Section 8 (pp. 20-24) define superinformation media and derive non-distinguishability, no-cloning of non-orthogonal states, complementarity and unpredictability from Principles I-IX. records.summary: Imported principles, audited and corrected against Deutsch and Marletto (2015, arXiv:1405.5563, Sections 3-6 pp. 9-12): a computation variable is a set S of at least two possible attributes for which all permutation tasks are possible with side-effects (Section 3 p. 9); a variable S is clonable if the cloning task R_S(x0) = union_{x in S} {(x, x0) -> (x, x)} is possible with side-effects for some preparable blank attribute x0 (Section 4 eq. (3) p. 10); an information variable is a clonable computation variable, and an information medium is a substrate with at least one information variable (Section 4 p. 10). Distinguishability is defined afterward in Section 5 (eq. (4) p. 11) by mapping into an information variable, avoiding circularity, and every information variable is then shown to be distinguishable. Principle III (interoperability, Section 6 p. 12) states that the composite S1 + S2 of two substrates with information variables S1 and S2 is an information medium with information variable S1 x S2.

records.summary: Marletto (2016, arXiv:1507.03287) formulates unpredictability in superinformation media via the non-existence of an X-predictor constructor (Section 4 pp. 21-22), defines X-indistinguishability equivalence classes and X-partitions of unity [f(z)_x] through the limiting ensemble fraction constructor D_x^(N) under conditions E1-E2 (Section 5 pp. 23-29), and shows that in a decision-supporting superinformation theory (conditions T1-T2 and R1-R4, Table 1 p. 32) a player automaton Gamma satisfying decision axioms A1-A2 (Section 6.2 pp. 35-36) values an X-game of chance G_X(y) by the additive expectation V{G_X(y)} = sum_{x in X} f(y)_x x (Section 7 eqs. (16), (18), (20) pp. 41-47). This node records the paper's results.

records.name: Marletto 2016: constructor theory of thermodynamics
records.obligation: Record only. Audited against arXiv:1608.02625 Sections 5-7; the repository has no thermodynamic substrate or adiabatic-accessibility relation.
records.summary: Marletto (2016, v5 2017, arXiv:1608.02625) defines work media as substrates with at least three equally-spaced energy attributes admitting an adjacent-pair swap on two replicas (so work variables are information variables by Principle VII, Section 5 pp. 27-31), states the First Law as interoperability of work media (Law I, eq. (4) p. 32), and defines adiabatic possibility {x -> y} as possibility with side-effects on work variables only (Section 5.3 p. 33). Section 6 (pp. 34-42) defines heat media, Principle IX (interoperability of heat media, p. 38), the Second Law (Law II, p. 39: existence of heat attributes h1, h2 with {h1 -> h2} adiabatically possible and {h2 -> h1} not adiabatically possible), an entropy function via the adiabatic 'is-like' relation (pp. 39-41), and the Zeroth Law (Law X, p. 42), deriving Kelvin's statement in Section 7 (pp. 42-44). This node records the paper's results.

records.name: Marletto-Vedral and Bose et al. 2017: gravitationally mediated entanglement witness
records.obligation: Record only. Audited against arXiv:1707.06036 and arXiv:1707.06050; the repository makes no physical claim about gravity.
records.summary: Marletto and Vedral (2017, arXiv:1707.06036, pp. 1-4, Fig. 1) argue within constructor theory that if a mediator M locally couples two quantum systems Q1 and Q2 (via Q1 <-> M <-> Q2 with no direct Q1-Q2 coupling) and generates entanglement from a product state, then M must carry at least two incompatible observables (a superinformation medium), and propose testing gravitationally induced phases between two interferometric masses; Bose et al. (2017, arXiv:1707.06050, pp. 1-5, eqs. (1)-(8)) independently propose a spin-correlation entanglement witness W = |(sigma_x^(1) tensor sigma_z^(2)) + (sigma_y^(1) tensor sigma_y^(2))| > 1 (eq. (8) p. 4) for two Stern-Gerlach interferometers interacting through Newtonian gravity phases delta phi_+- and delta phi_-+ (eqs. (2)-(4) p. 2). This node records both papers; no experiment is claimed to have been performed.

records.name: Imported inference: entanglement through a mediator indicates a non-classical mediator
records.obligation: The inference (arXiv:1707.06036 pp. 2-3; arXiv:1707.06050 pp. 1-2) is an assumption of this branch. It does not use or support any repository Lean result.
records.summary: Imported inference, audited against Marletto-Vedral (2017, arXiv:1707.06036, pp. 2-3) and Bose et al. (2017, arXiv:1707.06050, pp. 1-2): if two quantum systems Q1 and Q2 start in a separable state, interact only locally through a mediating system M (Q1 <-> M and M <-> Q2, with no direct Q1-Q2 interaction, Principle I locality), and end in an entangled state of Q1 + Q2, then M cannot be a classical medium (in Marletto-Vedral, M must have at least two disjoint incompatible observables whose union is not an information variable; in Bose et al., any mediator modeled by local operations and classical communication cannot create entanglement). The repository has no gravity model; TFQ-0084 is a finite shadow only.

records.name: Finite target: a phase interaction entangles; local operations do not
records.obligation: Statement (d), an exact separating functional on the 4x4 density matrix relative to the product family in the form of DS-QM071, is not proved. The Lean module defines schmidtWitnessExpectation(M) = |det M|^2, a quadratic function of the amplitude matrix that vanishes on product vectors and is positive on psi_u for u != 1; that is a restatement of (a), not a linear functional on density matrices, and it is not shown to vanish on mixtures of product states or tied to DS-QM071. The rank inequality rank(A M B^T) <= rank(M) for general rank is stated only through the 2x2 determinant identity (preservation of det M = 0). No physical claim is attached.
records.summary: Finite statement over Q(i), checked in Lean 4 for (a) to (c); (d) is not proved. For u in Q(i) (the Lean proofs of (a) and (b) do not use |u|=1), the two-qubit vector psi_u = (1,1,1,u)/2 has coefficient matrix M_u = [[1,1],[1,u]]/2 of determinant (u-1)/4. (a) psi_u is a product vector if and only if u=1. (b) The squared concurrence, defined as 4|det M|^2, equals |u-1|^2/4 for M_u; for u=(3+4i)/5, where |u|=1, it equals 1/5. (c) For all 2x2 matrices A and B over Q(i), det(A M B^T) = det(A) det(M) det(B), so det M = 0 implies det(A M B^T) = 0: local operations cannot raise a product vector to Schmidt rank 2; and diag(1,1,1,u) applied to the product vector (1,1,1,1)/2 gives psi_u. The physical inference from such entanglement to a non-classical mediator is imported, not part of this target.

records.name: Finite strict posets and spacelike separation in CausalOrder.lean
records.obligation: The theorem name incomparability_not_transitive_c1 overstates its statement. A genuine non-transitive example (the four-element N poset) is part of the finite net target of this stage.
records.summary: lean4/CausalOrder.lean defines FiniteStrictPoset n (an irreflexive transitive relation on Fin n) and spacelike separation (x differs from y and neither precedes the other). It establishes spacelike_symm and spacelike_irrefl; on the named examples C1 (0<1, 0<2) and C2 (the four-element diamond) it establishes c1_spacelike_1_2, c2_causal_0_3, order_independence_witness (C1 and its dual differ) and the table entries c1_mu_spacelike_vanishes and c2_mu_top_bottom (value 1). Scope: three decided examples, no general causal-set theory. The theorem named incomparability_not_transitive_c1 states only that e1 and e2 are spacelike in both orders and that e1 is not spacelike to itself; it does not exhibit a failure of transitivity of spacelike separation. The table c2_mu is checked entry by entry; the Lean file does not state the Mobius recursion for it.

records.name: Product tables are no-signalling in NoSignallingCore.lean
records.obligation: The quantum statement that commuting local measurements at spacelike separated points give setting-independent marginals is not stated in this file.
records.summary: lean4/NoSignallingCore.lean establishes, for natural-number-valued tables of the product form P x y a b = PA x a * PB y b in which each PB y sums to 1 over a listed outcome set, that the marginal on the first party does not depend on the second party's setting (product_noSignalling, marginalA_product), and that the table sig, in which the first outcome equals the second setting, has a setting-dependent marginal, so NoSignallingBA fails (sig_signals). records.name: Haag and Kastler 1964: local nets of observable algebras
records.obligation: Record only. The checkout holds no copy of the 1964 print article; the standard postulate list is checked in secondary sources (arXiv:math-ph/9903028 Section 1 pp. 2-3; arXiv:1607.03901 Section 6 pp. 28-30), while the primary 1964 numbering remains to be audited against the print text.
records.summary: Haag and Kastler (1964) formulate quantum field theory through a net that assigns to bounded spacetime regions the algebras of observables localized there, with the standard structural requirements later grouped as isotony (larger regions have larger algebras), locality (algebras of spacelike separated regions commute) and Poincare covariance, and with states as positive functionals. This node records the framework; the paper's own list of postulates is not reproduced.

records.name: Imported: a causal spacetime with a net of local algebras
records.obligation: The counts and products are one supplied four-point order and four supplied integer matrices. They are not a net indexed by continuum regions and not a Minkowski light cone. The Haag-Kastler import and the external light-cone lift named by DS-QM033-064-074-083-QHELD-CONTINUUM stay open. CausalOrder.lean is not a premise of a continuum theorem in this record.
records.summary: On the four-point strict order with the ordered relations 0<2, 1<2 and 1<3, the scan of all 64 triples holds, no point is related to itself, there are exactly 3 ordered relations, and exactly 3 of the 6 unordered pairs are spacelike: {0,1}, {0,3} and {2,3}. For the integer matrices A=[[1,2],[3,4]], B=[[5,6],[7,8]], X=[[0,1],[1,0]] and Z=[[1,0],[0,-1]], both (A tensor I)(I tensor B) and (I tensor B)(A tensor I) equal A tensor B, whose sixteen entries sum to 260. The products (X tensor I)(Z tensor I) and (Z tensor I)(X tensor I) differ, their (0,2) entries are -1 and 1, and XZ+ZX is the zero matrix. The determinants are det A = -2, det B = -2, det X = -1 and det Z = -1. A net of unital star-algebras indexed by continuum regions, and a Minkowski light cone, stay imported. This record does not import CausalOrder.lean and does not transport these finite counts to a continuum net.

records.name: Finite target: isotony and locality for a net on a finite poset
records.obligation: Not proved in Lean: the statements for the full local matrix algebras A(O) (linear spans of elementary tensors, for example 2^|O| x 2^|O| matrices): that commutation of elementary tensors extends by bilinearity to the algebras and that A(O1) is a subalgebra of A(O2) as matrix algebras; the single-site monoid M is generic and is not instantiated at 2x2 matrices. The net is kinematical: dynamics, a time-slice property and covariance are not modelled, so the statement is the finite shadow of two axioms and nothing more.
records.summary: Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 for site-factorized operators. For a FiniteStrictPoset P on n points put one qubit (a single-site monoid M) at each point; an operator A : Fin n -> M is localized in a subset O of P when it is the identity outside O, so the Lean "algebra" of O is the set of elementary tensor operators localized in O, not the full matrix algebra on the qubits in O. (a) Isotony: O1 inside O2 and A localized in O1 imply A localized in O2. (b) Locality: if every point of O1 is spacelike to every point of O2, then O1 and O2 are disjoint and operators localized in O1 and in O2 commute under the sitewise product. (c) The spacelike relation of CausalOrder.lean is symmetric (spacelike_symm) and irreflexive (spacelike_irrefl) and not transitive: on the four-element N poset 0<2, 1<2, 1<3, points 1 and 0 are spacelike, 0 and 3 are spacelike, and 1<3 are related. The content of Haag-Kastler locality (commutation forced by causal separation of dynamics) is absent because this net has no dynamics.

records.name: Reeh and Schlieder 1961: cyclicity of the vacuum
records.obligation: Record only. The precise hypotheses (spectrum condition, vacuum uniqueness, covariance) are to be audited against the paper.
records.summary: Reeh and Schlieder (1961) study the unitary equivalence of Lorentz-invariant fields and obtain what is cited as the Reeh-Schlieder property: for a positive-energy, Poincare covariant theory with a vacuum vector, the vacuum is cyclic for the algebra of any bounded open region. The paper is in German and the checkout holds no copy; the statement and hypotheses are recorded from citations.

records.name: Imported: Reeh-Schlieder property and its continuum hypotheses
records.obligation: The inputs of the property are the continuum Hilbert lift and the Stone theorem, which the repository records as open. The gap route below lists them.
records.summary: Imported property: in a net of local algebras on Minkowski space with a translation action whose generators have positive spectrum (spectrum condition) and a vacuum vector, the vacuum is cyclic for every local algebra, and under further hypotheses separating for the algebra of a region with spacelike complement. The proof uses analytic continuation of translations, hence a continuous translation group and its generator (Stone's theorem) on an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. Both are open nodes of the repository.

records.name: Finite target: cyclicity of a state for a subsystem algebra is a rank condition
records.obligation: Not proved in Lean: separating implies full column rank (so the three-way equivalence is not complete); the identification of full column rank with full rank of the reduced state; the qubit subset bookkeeping; the conclusion "not cyclic" for the single-site cases (cyclic implies left inverse is proved only for dB <= dA, and a single site has dA=2 < dB=4; the kernel vectors give non-separating only) and for |000> on pairs (a zero column is exhibited but "zero column implies no left inverse implies not cyclic" is not stated as a theorem); that |000> is cyclic for the full algebra. A Lean proof of the equivalence for general n is open. The relation to the continuum theorem is an analogy: finite dimension has no translation group or spectrum condition.
records.summary: Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 in the following narrowed form. Let Omega be a dA x dB matrix over a semiring R (the amplitude matrix of a vector in H_A tensor H_{A^c}; for qubits dA = 2^|A| and dB = 2^|A^c|, but the qubit tensor-factor bookkeeping is not formalised). Omega is cyclic for End(H_A) when every dA x dB matrix is X Omega for some X. (a) If Omega has a left inverse L with L Omega = I_dB (full column rank dB, which over a field is full rank of the reduced state on A^c) then Omega is cyclic and Omega is separating for End(H_{A^c}) (Omega Y = 0 implies Y = 0). (b) Conversely, cyclic implies a left inverse whenever dB <= dA (an injection Fin dB -> Fin dA is supplied). (c) A nonzero vector in the right kernel of Omega makes Omega not separating. (d) Exact 3-qubit instances over Z for the product vector |000>, GHZ = |000>+|111> and W = |100>+|010>+|001>: explicit nonzero right-kernel vectors for every single-site unfolding (2 x 4), explicit integer left inverses of every pair-of-sites unfolding (4 x 2) for GHZ and W, and a zero column in every pair-of-sites unfolding of |000>.

records.name: Epstein and Glaser 1973: the role of locality in perturbation theory
records.obligation: Record only. Audited against the Numdam full text (AIHPA_1973__19_3_211_0); nothing in the paper is used as a premise of a repository theorem.
records.summary: Epstein and Glaser (1973, Ann. Inst. H. Poincare A 19, 211-295, Abstract p. 211, Section 1.1 pp. 214-215, Section 2.1 eq. (9) p. 218, Section 2.2 eq. (30) p. 223, and Section 5 pp. 231-237) give an inductive construction of the perturbation series S(g) = 1 + sum_{n>=1} (i^n / n!) int T_n(x_1,...,x_n) g(x_1)...g(x_n) dx in which each order T_n is constructed from lower orders by causal factorization outside the total diagonal and by splitting causal distributions with scaling degree bounds on the diagonal. This node records the paper as published.

records.name: Imported: causal factorization of the scattering matrix
records.obligation: Audited against Epstein-Glaser (1973) eqs. (9), (30) and Brunetti-Fredenhagen (2000) eq. (2) and Condition P3. The continuum distribution extension has no counterpart in the repository's finite posets.
records.summary: Imported property, audited and corrected against Epstein and Glaser (1973, Section 1.1 condition (C.A.) pp. 214-215, Section 2.1 condition (Caus. 1) eq. (9) p. 218, Section 2.2 eq. (30) p. 223) and Brunetti and Fredenhagen (2000, arXiv:math-ph/9903028, Section 1 eq. (2) p. 4 and Section 3 Condition P3 p. 15): the scattering operator satisfies V(g, h1+h2) = S(g)^{-1} S(g+h1+h2) = V(g, h1) V(g, h2) (and at g=0, S(g1+g2) = S(g1) S(g2)) whenever supp h1 does not intersect the causal past of supp h2, written supp h1 cap (supp h2 + V^-) = empty (which includes spacelike separation as well as causal future separation, not only supp h1 inside the causal future of supp h2). Equivalently at each order n, the time-ordered operator-valued distributions factorize as T(P union Q) = T(P) T(Q) whenever {x_i : i in P} cap ({x_j : j in Q} + V^-) = empty (eq. (30) p. 223; Condition P3 p. 15), and renormalization reduces to extending time-ordered products across the total diagonal. The repository has neither operator-valued distributions nor a continuum Minkowski causal cone. Narrowed in Lean 4 and an independent Python verifier to three exact finite/algebraic components and non-equivalence fences: (1) over any group G and additive coupling carrier A, the relative Bogoliubov operator bogoliubovV S g h = (S g)^{-1} * S(g + h) satisfies V(g, 0) = 1, the unconditional telescoping cocycle law V(g, h1) * V(g + h1, h2) = V(g, h1 + h2), and the equivalence V(g, h1 + h2) = V(g, h1) * V(g, h2) <-> V(g + h1, h2) = V(g, h2), while on the diamond poset C2 the Epstein-Glaser separation predicate noInCausalPast C2 holds symmetrically for spacelike ([d1], [d2]) and one-way for future-before-past ([d1, d2, d3], [d0]); (2) on the 4-element N poset (0 < 2, 1 < 2, 1 < 3), all 5 linear extensions extN0..extN4 are connected by chains of adjacent spacelike swaps (SpacelikeSwapChain posetN) and have identical ordered products for every spacelike-commuting monoid assignment (discharging the finite-poset connectivity question of TFQ-2110), while anticommuting Pauli operators X, Z on (n0, n3) flip the sign between extN3 and extN4; and (3) coincident pairs (x, x) on a FiniteStrictPoset are never spacelike separated, the 4D Epstein-Glaser polynomial counterterm dimension binom(omega + 4, 4) equals (1, 5, 15, 35, 70) for omega = 0..4, and off-diagonal factorization (x != y) leaves coincident-diagonal contact counterterms c unconstrained.

records.name: Finite target: time-ordered products over linear extensions of a poset
records.obligation: Not proved in Lean: that any two linear extensions of an arbitrary finite strict poset are connected by a chain of adjacent spacelike swaps, which is the step that turns swap invariance into independence from the choice of linear extension. Connectivity is exhibited for the two extensions of C2 only; for the N poset the five extensions are counted but their connectivity, and hence the equality of their ordered products, is not stated. The relation to Epstein-Glaser is an analogy.
records.summary: Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 in the following narrowed form. For a FiniteStrictPoset P and elements A_x (x in P) of a monoid with A_x A_y = A_y A_x for all spacelike pairs x,y: the ordered product along a listing of P is unchanged by one adjacent swap of spacelike elements, hence by any chain of adjacent spacelike swaps. Exact checks: the diamond C2 has exactly 2 linear extensions among the 24 permutations of its four points, [0,1,2,3] and [0,2,1,3], connected by one adjacent spacelike swap of 1 and 2; the N poset has exactly 5 linear extensions; with integer 2x2 Pauli matrices on C2 the two ordered products agree when the spacelike points 1 and 2 carry the commuting matrices Z and Z, and differ by the sign -1 (and are unequal) when they carry the anticommuting matrices X and Z. The distribution extension and the ultraviolet content of the Epstein-Glaser construction have no finite counterpart.

records.name: Bombelli, Lee, Meyer and Sorkin 1987: space-time as a causal set
records.obligation: Record only. Sorkin (2003, arXiv:gr-qc/0309009 Section 3 p. 6) and Reid (2003, arXiv:gr-qc/0207103 Section II p. 2) were audited in full; the 1987 PRL print article is not held in the checkout.
records.summary: Bombelli, Lee, Meyer and Sorkin (1987) propose that spacetime at the smallest scales is a discrete structure, a causal set: a locally finite set with a partial order encoding past and future. They examine how a Lorentzian manifold can approximate such a set, note that effective dimensionality can vary with length scale, and sketch a quantum dynamics. Sorkin's Valdivia notes (2003) are a later survey. This node records the proposal.

records.name: A finite causal set is a FiniteStrictPoset
records.obligation: Definitional only. Nothing about manifold-likeness, dimension or the continuum limit is asserted.
records.summary: Reading of definitions. A causal set in the sense of the source is a locally finite partially ordered set; in the strict-order form its relation is irreflexive and transitive, and local finiteness is automatic on a finite set. This is the structure FiniteStrictPoset n of lean4/CausalOrder.lean. The Python class CausalSet in code/python/src/general_relativity/causal_set.py builds a poset from relations, takes the transitive closure and refuses cycles. The identification involves no sprinkling, no embedding in a Lorentzian manifold and no dynamics.

records.name: Finite target: ordering fraction, Myrheim-Meyer dimension and Hasse diagrams as exact rationals
records.obligation: Not proved in Lean: that the n x n grid poset (a FiniteStrictPoset on n^2 points) has R(n) strictly related pairs, so (i) is arithmetic on a posited count cross-checked against the diamond only at n=2; the derivation of f(d) from the Gamma-function formula; correctness of the nearest-dimension selector beyond the six listed inputs; that the Hasse relation itself generates the order and is the minimal such relation. Everything is rational arithmetic on named finite posets. The dimension estimator is a heuristic for sprinklings; the finite estimate on a small poset carries no manifold statement.
records.summary: Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 in the following narrowed form. The ordering fraction of a finite causal set is the exact rational r = 2R/(n(n-1)), with R the number of strictly related pairs (CausalSet.ordering_fraction); Lean computes r(C1)=2/3 and r(C2)=5/6 from the relation tables of CausalOrder.lean. In Sorkin (2003, arXiv:gr-qc/0309009 Section 7 p. 16), the expected ordering fraction of a Poisson sprinkling into a d-dimensional Minkowski causal interval normalized by binom(N,2) is f(d) = (3/2) Gamma(d+1) Gamma(d/2 + 1) / Gamma(3d/2 + 1) = Gamma(d+1) Gamma(d/2) / (2 Gamma(3d/2)) (in Reid 2003, arXiv:gr-qc/0207103 Section III eq. (5) p. 5, normalizing by <N>^2 instead of binom(N,2) gives f(d)/2 = Gamma(d+1) Gamma(d/2) / (4 Gamma(3d/2))), with exact rational values f(1)=1, f(2)=1/2, f(3)=8/35 and f(4)=1/10; in Lean these four values are entered as a table (70 f(d) = 70, 35, 16, 7) and not derived from the Gamma formula. (i) If the n x n grid with the componentwise product order has R(n) = (n(n+1)/2)^2 - n^2 strictly related pairs (a count entered as a definition in Lean, not derived from a poset), then 4 R(n) = n^2 (n-1)(n+3), the ordering fraction is r = (n+3)/(2(n+1)) for all n >= 2 with r(n) - 1/2 = 1/(n+1), the values for n=2..6 are 5/6, 3/4, 7/10, 2/3, 9/14, and r(2) = 5/6 equals the exactly computed r(C2) of the diamond. This is an observation about a lattice, not an instance of the sprinkling theorem. (ii) An exact nearest-dimension selector over d in {1,2,3,4} with tie reporting is defined and checked on the six inputs 5/6, 3/4, 7/10, 1/2, 8/35, 1/10, giving [1], [1,2] (an exact tie), [2], [2], [3], [4]. (iii) The Hasse covering relation of any FiniteStrictPoset is contained in every subrelation E of the order such that every related pair is in E or has an intermediate element (one half of "unique transitive reduction"); C1 has 2 links and C2 has 4; the Mobius tables c1_mu and c2_mu of CausalOrder.lean satisfy the Mobius recursion and c2_mu(d0,d3)=1.

records.name: Maldacena 1997: large N superconformal field theories and supergravity
records.obligation: Record only. The duality is a conjecture supported by checks in the source literature.

records.name: Gubser-Klebanov-Polyakov and Witten 1998: the correlator dictionary

records.name: Ryu and Takayanagi 2006: holographic entanglement entropy

records.summary: Ryu and Takayanagi (2006, arXiv:hep-th/0603001, Section 1 eq. records.name: Imported: entropy of a boundary region equals minimal surface area over 4G

records.summary: Imported formula, as the source states it at leading order in Newton's constant: S(A) = Area(minimal surface anchored on the boundary of A) / (4 G). It presupposes the von Neumann entropy of a boundary reduced state on a continuum Hilbert space and the area of a surface in a bulk geometry. The repository has an exact von Neumann entropy dichotomy for algebraic spectra and an exact rational Regge area proxy that is not the Einstein-Hilbert action; neither is a minimal-surface area in a bulk geometry. Narrowed in Lean 4 and an independent Python verifier to three exact finite/rational algebraic shadows and scope fences: (1) over Q, substituting the regulated AdS_3 geodesic length 2 R_AdS * logFactor into rtLeadingEntropy(area, G_N) = area / (4 G_N) reproduces the 2D CFT Calabrese-Cardy coefficient (c / 3) * logFactor under the Brown-Henneaux relation c = 3 R_AdS / (2 G_N^(3)) and eliminates both bulk couplings in S_A / c = logFactor / 3, while submodular surface pasting yields Strong Subadditivity S(ABC) + S(B) <= S(AB) + S(BC) and all 380 proper contiguous boundary intervals of the 20-qubit 6-pentagon HaPPY patch satisfy complement symmetry A <-> A^c; (2) under BakerCitedInput (EntropyDichotomy.lean), no mixed algebraic spectrum can have natural-log von Neumann entropy equal to a rational RT ratio area / (4 G_N), equality holds at G_N > 0 iff the state is pure and area = 0, and stabilizer bit counts require dividing by log 2; and (3) on the orthogonal_pentatope chart of TFQ-0100, the 6 right-triangle hinges have Cayley-Menger squared area 1/4 and the 4 equilateral-triangle hinges have squared area 3/4 (total 9/2) with no rational linear area A in Q satisfying A^2 = 3/4, the flat-chart Regge proxy (kappa = 0) vanishes identically whereas all 380 HaPPY intervals satisfy 1 <= S(A) <= mincut(A), and under length rescaling L -> lam * L the Regge proxy scales as lam^4 against lam^2 for 2-surface area and lam^0 for bond counts.

records.summary: Harlow (2016, arXiv:1607.03901, Theorem 1.1 pp. 3-4 and Section 5 Theorem 5.1 pp. 20-26) establishes in finite-dimensional operator-algebra quantum error correction that for a code subspace H_code in H_A tensor H_{A-bar} and a von Neumann algebra M on H_code with commutant M' and center Z_M = M cap M', three conditions are equivalent: (i) complementary recovery of M on A and M' on A-bar, (ii) existence of a positive central area operator L_A in Z_M such that for every code state rho-tilde, S(rho-tilde_A) = Tr(rho-tilde L_A) + S(rho-tilde, M) and S(rho-tilde_{A-bar}) = Tr(rho-tilde L_A) + S(rho-tilde, M'), and (iii) conservation of relative entropy S(rho-tilde_A | sigma-tilde_A) = S(rho-tilde | sigma-tilde, M). This node records the paper as published.

records.name: Finite target: the five-qubit code gives a six-leg perfect tensor
records.obligation: Checked in Lean 4 by exhaustive GF(2) symplectic enumeration over the 64-element stabilizer group, the 20 bipartitions and the 1024-element five-qubit Pauli group. A finite stabilizer enumeration is not a statement about AdS/CFT.
records.summary: Formalized finite statement. The [[5,1,3]] code of Laflamme, Miquel, Paz and Zurek has stabilizer generators XZZXI, IXZZX, XIXZZ, ZXIXZ and logical operators XXXXX and ZZZZZ. Its Choi state is the six-qubit stabilizer state with generators g tensor I (four of them), XXXXX tensor X and ZZZZZ tensor Z. Checked in Lean 4 on Pauli operators modulo phase (GF(2) symplectic vectors): the six generators pairwise commute and generate a group of 64 distinct elements, with weight distribution 1 element of weight 0, 45 of weight 4 and 18 of weight 6 (the hexacode six-qubit state), so every non-identity element has weight at least 4, which is the perfect-tensor condition (every bipartition with at most three legs on one side has a maximally mixed marginal); for all twenty 3|3 bipartitions the stabilizer subgroup supported on one side is trivial, so the entropy is 3 bits by the stabilizer formula S(A) = |A| - log2 |G_A|; and in the five-qubit code the normalizer of the 16-element stabilizer has order 64 and its 48 elements outside the stabilizer (the nontrivial logical operators, modulo phase) have minimum weight 3. The reading of weights and local stabilizer subgroups as marginals and entropies is the standard stabilizer-formalism dictionary and is not formalised on density matrices.

records.name: Finite target: boundary entropies of a six-tensor patch against minimal cuts
records.obligation: Not proved in Lean: that the 20 explicit generators are the boundary stabilizer of the contracted six-tensor network with bulk legs fixed at logical zero (they are entered by hand from the pushing rules of the code generators); that mincut as computed (a minimum over side assignments of the six tensors) is the minimal curve cut in the planar dual; the list of the 40 intervals where equality fails (only the counts are stated). The correspondence to a continuum minimal-surface area is the imported formula and is not part of the target.
records.summary: Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 for a hand-encoded model. Contract six copies of the six-leg perfect tensor on the {5,4} pentagon tiling: one central tensor and its five edge-neighbours, which are not adjacent to each other, so the patch has 20 dangling boundary legs (4 per outer tensor) and 6 bulk legs, every bulk leg fixed in the logical zero state. In Lean the 20-qubit boundary stabilizer is given by 20 explicit generators (15 local to the five outer blocks and 5 pushed through the internal bonds from the central tensor): they pairwise commute and have full GF(2) rank 20. For all 380 proper contiguous boundary intervals A (20 starting positions, lengths 1 to 19), with S(A) = rank(G restricted to A) - |A| in bits and mincut(A) the minimal number of bonds cut separating A from its complement in the six-tensor star graph: S(A) <= mincut(A) on all 380 intervals, S(A) = mincut(A) on exactly 340 intervals, and S(A) = mincut(A) - 1 on exactly 40. The Ryu-Takayanagi equality therefore fails on this patch for 40 intervals; it is not a statement that holds for every region.

records.name: Finite target: logical operators of the five-qubit code live on any three qubits
records.obligation: Checked in Lean 4 over the 16-element stabilizer, its three logical cosets, all 10 triples, all 10 pairs and all 105 low-weight Pauli errors. The identification with bulk operator reconstruction in AdS/CFT is the imported picture of the source.
records.summary: Formalized finite statement. For the [[5,1,3]] code, each of the ten 3-qubit subsets T of physical qubits supports a representative of each of the three nontrivial logical classes (the cosets of the stabilizer by XXXXX, ZZZZZ and YYYYY, the product class), and no 2-qubit subset supports a representative of any of them. Equivalent statement also checked in Lean 4: all 105 non-identity Pauli errors of weight 1 or 2 anticommute with a stabilizer generator, so none lies in the normalizer and erasure of any two qubits is correctable (the Knill-Laflamme condition). All operators are Pauli operators modulo phase. This is the smallest exact instance of the subregion-reconstruction picture of bulk operators.

records.summary: Open question: whether the exact rational Regge proxy of TFQ-0100 (squared hinge areas weighted by a holonomy defect, which is not the Einstein-Hilbert action) can supply the area term of a finite minimal-surface statement. The imported formula uses the area of a minimal surface in a bulk geometry; the HaPPY patch measures a bond count (one bit per bond). Matching the two needs a dictionary from geometry to network that no source supplies. records.name: Gap: finite code checks are not a derivation of AdS/CFT
records.obligation: Recorded as an explicit non-claim and non-equivalence fence so that finite stabilizer-code checks are not read as evidence for continuum AdS/CFT; Lorentzian time evolution, non-flat entanglement spectra, sub-AdS locality, and continuum gravitational dynamics remain open.
records.summary: No source read for this change derives AdS/CFT, or its continuum entropy formula, from a finite stabilizer-code tensor network. The HaPPY codes are discrete kinematic models of the bulk-to-boundary map on a hyperbolic tiling with no Lorentzian time, no dynamics, no gravitational action and no large-N limit. Narrowed in Lean 4 and an independent Python verifier to three exact non-equivalence fences: (1) every stabilizer reduced state has flat Renyi spectrum S_n / S_1 = 1, whereas a 2D CFT single interval has Calabrese-Cardy / Ryu-Takayanagi Renyi ratio cftRenyiFactor(n) = (1 + 1/n)/2, yielding a strictly positive defect ((n - 1)/(2n)) * S_1 > 0 for all n > 1 and S_1 > 0; (2) on the 20-qubit boundary state of the 6-pentagon {5,4} HaPPY patch (with bulk legs fixed in |0_L>), all 280 contiguous intervals of lengths 1..7 and 13..19 satisfy S(A) = mincut(A), whereas lengths 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 exhibit 5, 10, 10, 10, 5 strict Ryu-Takayanagi deficits (S(A) = mincut(A) - 1, summing to 40), including the explicit 5-fold rotational orbit start = 4*k + 2 at len = 8 and its complement len = 12 (S = 4 < 5 = mincut); and (3) disconnected boundary regions exhibit discrete integer mutual-information jumps (0, 0, 3, 1 bits) while for nBulk < nBdry the bulk code subspace 2^{nBulk} has strictly positive orthogonal codimension 2^{nBdry} - 2^{nBulk} > 0 (30, 1048512, 33552384 for 1, 6, and 11 pentagons).

(21) and conditions i-ii p. 12), labelled by imbedded graphs whose edges carry SU(2) representations (twice-spins p_l) and whose higher-valence vertices carry virtual trivalent trees/intertwiners (Appendix A pp. 36-38), and show in Section 6 (pp. 26-29) that these spin-network states are orthonormal with respect to the Ashtekar-Lewandowski Haar measure. records.name: Rovelli-Smolin 1995 and Ashtekar-Lewandowski 1997: area and volume spectra
records.obligation: Record only. Both normalization conventions (l_P^2 vs 8 pi gamma l_P^2, per Ashtekar-Lewandowski Section 3.3 footnote 6 p. 16) and the general vertex-puncture formula (eq. (4.9) p. 18) were audited against the papers on 2026-10-22.
records.summary: Rovelli and Smolin (1995, arXiv:gr-qc/9411005, Section 1 eqs. (1)-(2) p. 4 and Section 4 eqs. (47)-(48) p. 28) and Ashtekar and Lewandowski (1997, arXiv:gr-qc/9602046, Section 3.3 eq. (3.20) p. 16 and Section 4.1 eqs. (4.7)-(4.9), (4.12) pp. 18-19) compute discrete spectra for loop-quantum-gravity area (and volume) operators. In the convention {A_a^i(x), E_j^b(y)} = G delta_a^b delta_j^i delta^3(x,y) used in both papers, the general area eigenvalue is (l_P^2 / 2) sum_v sqrt(2 j_v^(d)(j_v^(d)+1) + 2 j_v^(u)(j_v^(u)+1) - j_v^(d+u)(j_v^(d+u)+1)) (eq. (4.9) of gr-qc/9602046), which for simple transverse punctures without tangential edges (j^(d)=j^(u)=j_i, j^(d+u)=0) equals l_P^2 sum_i sqrt(j_i(j_i+1)) = (l_P^2 / 2) sum_i sqrt(p_i(p_i+2)) with p_i = 2 j_i (eq. (2) and eq. (47) of gr-qc/9411005; eq. (4.12) of gr-qc/9602046); as Ashtekar and Lewandowski note in Section 3.3 footnote 6 (p. 16) and Engle et al. write in arXiv:0711.0146 Section V eq. (36) (p. 11), restoring the 8 pi G gamma factor from the gravitational action and Barbero-Immirzi parameter gamma multiplies this spectrum by 8 pi gamma, giving 8 pi gamma l_P^2 sum_i sqrt(j_i(j_i+1)). (The nonzero trivalent volume formula in eq. (1) and eq. (37) of gr-qc/9411005 was corrected in the erratum Nucl. Phys. B 456 (1995) 753, where trivalent vertices have zero volume.) This node records both papers and their normalization conventions.

records.name: Ponzano and Regge 1968: semiclassical limit of Racah coefficients
records.obligation: Record only. The 1968 chapter has no arXiv record and is not held in the checkout; its asymptotic formula is verified in Roberts (1999, arXiv:math-ph/9812013 Theorem 1 p. 22 and Section 6.1 p. 61).
records.summary: Ponzano and Regge (1968) give the leading asymptotic form of the 6j symbol (Racah coefficient) for large spins, with separate forms for the classically allowed and forbidden regions, and introduce a state sum for three-dimensional gravity whose phase matches the Regge action of a tetrahedron. The formula was reached by conjecture and numerical checks. This node records the chapter by title and publication details.

records.name: Roberts 1999: classical 6j symbols and the tetrahedron
records.obligation: Record only. Audited against arXiv:math-ph/9812013 Theorem 1 eq. (2) p. 22 and Section 6.1 eqs. (12)-(13) p. 61 on 2026-10-22.
records.summary: Roberts (1999, arXiv:math-ph/9812013, Section 1 Theorem 1 eq. (2) p. 22 and Section 6.1 eqs. (12)-(13) p. 61) establishes by geometric quantization of the 8-sphere and stationary phase on the symplectic reduction that for an admissible 6-tuple of integers a, b, c, d, e, f (where a = 2j labels the (a+1)-dimensional irreducible representation of SU(2)) whose side lengths form a non-degenerate Euclidean tetrahedron tau of positive volume V(tau) > 0 and exterior dihedral angles theta_r, the rescaled 6j symbol {ka, kb, kc; kd, ke, kf} has the k -> infinity asymptotic expansion sqrt(2 / (3 pi V(tau) k^3)) cos(sum_{r=1}^6 (k a_r + 1) theta_r / 2 + pi/4) + O(k^{-5/2}). Since a tetrahedron of side lengths j_r = a_r/2 has volume V_j = V(tau)/8, substituting 2 / (3 pi V(tau)) = 1 / (12 pi V_j) and (a_r + 1)/2 = j_r + 1/2 recovers the Ponzano-Regge prefactor (12 pi V_j)^{-1/2}. This node records the paper's theorem.

records.name: Imported: Ponzano-Regge asymptotics of the 6j symbol
records.obligation: The asymptotic statement is a limit of real-valued quantities; the repository's exact finite targets do not establish a limit.
records.summary: Imported asymptotic form, audited against Roberts (1999, arXiv:math-ph/9812013, Theorem 1 eq. (2) p. 22 and Section 6.1 eqs. (12)-(13) p. 61): for large spins with edge lengths l_r = j_r + 1/2 = (a_r + 1)/2 (where a_r = 2 j_r), when the six lengths bound a non-degenerate Euclidean tetrahedron of positive volume V > 0 and exterior dihedral angles theta_r, the 6j symbol behaves asymptotically as (12 pi V)^{-1/2} cos(sum_{r=1}^6 (j_r + 1/2) theta_r + pi/4) (equivalently sqrt(2 / (3 pi V(a))) cos(sum_{r=1}^6 (a_r + 1) theta_r / 2 + pi/4) where V(a) = 8 V is the volume for side lengths a_r = 2 j_r), and decays exponentially when the Cayley-Menger squared volume is negative (Lorentzian tetrahedron, Section 6.2 p. 62). The phase is the Regge action of the tetrahedron.

records.summary: For rational gamma and rational k, the imported Euclidean labels are j+ = |1 + gamma| k / 2 and j- = |1 - gamma| k / 2. When 0 < gamma < 1 they equal (1 + gamma) k / 2 and (1 - gamma) k / 2, their sum is k, and their difference is gamma k. When gamma > 1 they equal (1 + gamma) k / 2 and (gamma - 1) k / 2, their difference is k, and their sum is gamma k. At gamma = 1/2 and k = 2 the labels are 3/2 and 1/2, the sum is 2, and the difference is 1, which is not 2. At gamma = 3 and k = 2 the labels are 4 and 2, the difference is 2, and the sum is 6, which is not 2. At gamma = 1 and k = 2 the labels are 2 and 0, and both the sum and the difference equal 2. The imported Lorentzian pair is (n, rho) = (2 k, 2 gamma k), with rho = gamma n = 2 gamma (n / 2). At gamma = 1/2 and k = 2 this pair is (4, 2), the index j = n / 2 equals 2, and gamma j equals 1, so rho = 2 gamma j rather than gamma j. The number of unordered pairs among five indices is 10. A Spin(4) 15j contraction, booster factors, a continuum Lie-group representation, a spin-network boundary space, a sum over spins, a continuum limit, a semiclassical limit, and a cosmological constant stay imported and are not constructed.
